slides.title: ADHD + a tidy partner: the things that ended our cleaning fights
Split by task, not by 'help'
slides.body: 'Can you help more?' is vague. 'I do dishes, you do laundry' is clear. Each person owns tasks start to finish.

slides.title: Pick tasks that fit your brain
slides.body: Some of us love quick wins, some like long tasks with a podcast. Trade so each person gets the type they can stick with.

slides.title: Agree on 'good enough'
slides.body: Write down what 'done' means for each room. It stops the 'you call that clean?' fights.

slides.title: Ask for a reminder, not a lecture
slides.body: Agree on one short phrase, like 'laundry check?'. Neutral words, no sighs.

slides.title: Give your stuff a drop zone
slides.body: A basket or shelf where your stuff can land without judgment. It keeps shared spaces calm.

slides.title: We weren't fighting about dishes. We were fighting about feeling unseen.
A plan you can share
slides.body: The Messy Brain Home Reset gives you both a clear 7-day plan to split. Link in bio.
